beats.text: Fourteen days of Play Tennis. On nine days they played. On five, they did not. A decision tree will predict the answer by asking one question at a time.
But which question comes first? Outlook, humidity, wind, or temperature?
A good question leaves each group pure: all yes, or all no. Entropy measures how mixed a group is.
A pure group, all one class, has entropy zero. There is nothing left to ask.
A fifty fifty group has entropy one bit. That is the worst case. You know nothing about the answer.
In between, entropy climbs from zero to its peak at fifty fifty, and falls back to zero.
Our fourteen days, nine yes and five no, are quite mixed: zero point nine four zero bits.
Now try outlook. Sunny gets two yes and three no. Overcast gets four yes, and no no at all. Rain gets three yes and two no.
Overcast is pure: entropy zero. Sunny and rain are mixed: zero point nine seven one each.
Weight each child by its size: five out of fourteen, four out of fourteen, five out of fourteen. Together they leave zero point six nine four.
Entropy fell from zero point nine four zero to zero point six nine four. That drop, about zero point two four six, is the information gain.
Humidity would leave zero point seven eight eight. Wind, zero point eight nine two. Temperature, zero point nine one one. Outlook leaves the least, so outlook becomes the root.
Then repeat inside every branch that is still mixed. Sunny asks about humidity. Rain asks about wind.
The slides stop when a leaf holds a single example, or when splitting would raise the entropy.
A tree grown too far starts to fit noise. Pruning cuts it back, and the tree is judged on new examples.
For the exam.
Entropy measures how mixed a node is.
Pure is zero. Fifty fifty is one bit, the worst.
Weight each child by its size.
Choose the split with the largest gain.
On Play Tennis, outlook wins.
